rationale: Greek loanword γνόφος/κνέφας 'gloom, dense darkness.' Used here in cosmological-meteorological register: 'the gloom of wind' as one of the Virgin-of-Light's three signs, distinct from Manichaean ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ 'Darkness' (cosmic principle). Captures the obscuring-but-mobile quality of wind-driven dark cloud.

Doublet-partner of ⲟⲩⲍⲣⲁⲕ 'stillness' in the formula 'in stillness and ⲟⲩϫⲁⲙⲏ' that recurs at lines 18-19 of this page describing Virgin-of-Light's tranquil sign. Likely Coptic ϭⲁⲙⲏ 'silence, calm.' Confidence moderate; flag for parallels.

Plural noun paired with ⲛⲓⲧⲏⲩ 'the winds' in line 6. Likely a Lycopolitan term for wind-blasts/gusts/storms. Etymology unclear; may relate to ⲱⲥⲙⲉ 'be strong' or to a windy-blowing root. Confidence low.

Lycopolitan ⲥⲙⲉⲓⲛⲉ likely = Sahidic ⲥⲙⲏ-ⲛⲉ or ⲙⲁⲉⲓⲛ 'sign, mark.' Recurs four times on this page (lines 4, 17 ×2, 25) as the technical term for each Virgin-of-Light's distinguishing sign. Direct correspondential register: each cloud-formation IS the sign of the Virgin.
Verbal compound ⲣ̄- + ⲍⲁⲓⲙⲉ (Lyc. for ϩⲟⲉⲓⲙ 'wave,' cf. glossary ⲍⲓⲙⲉⲩⲉ). Cosmographic verb describing the cloud-and-wind agitating the rivers and seas as it descends from the Virgin's domain.

Lexeme of uncertain identity in line 22. Editor restored ⲗⲟⲥ ending. Possibly a Lyc./scribal variant of ⲁⲅⲅⲉⲗⲟⲥ 'angels' (with ⲣⲧ for ⲅⲅ via metathesis), or an unidentified Greek-derived term. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.
